category_frame: the category you want to own, e.g. 'household bill tracker'
not_positioned_as: the adjacent category to explicitly avoid, e.g. 'budgeting app'
icp: one sentence describing who this is for, as specific as possible
canonical_definition_sentence: One sentence defining the product/business. Reused verbatim in meta description, schema description, and every article's first paragraph.

real_differentiators: a plain string = true and available on every tier/plan

real_differentiators.feature: a feature that's real but only on one plan, e.g. team invites or multi-user sharing
real_differentiators.tier: name the specific plan here, e.g. 'family plan only' — never leave this vague

coming_soon_features: list features that exist in code/roadmap but are NOT available yet — articles must never claim these are live

pricing_and_billing.note: state the ACTUAL billing mechanics here, e.g. 'pay-now with a 30-day money-back guarantee, NOT a free trial' — this is the single most common content-accuracy bug: copy drifting from real billing reality

claim_evidence.claim: The exact product claim this source verifies.

application_category: the most specific schema.org applicationCategory value that fits, e.g. FinanceApplication

image_style.accent_color: the site's real brand accent hex, e.g. #0d9488 — reused as the single accent color in every generated image for house-style consistency
image_style.palette: describe the rest of the palette, e.g. 'warm-neutral: cream, charcoal, walnut wood'
image_style.notes: see IMAGES.md before generating anything — the prompt pattern that avoids garbled pseudo-text is to describe every paper/screen as blank, closed, or face-down, not just to say 'no text'

current_month_year: Month Year — set this per generation
facts_last_verified: YYYY-MM-DD — set this whenever you (re)confirm verified_facts against the live site. scripts/check_article.py WARNs once this is more than 30 days old.
